## Assertions

- Release assets are generated from v* tags and dry-run built on pull requests.
- Provider CLIs and secrets are never bundled in riido-daemon release archives.
- GitHub Releases are the immutable daemon binary source; CDN latest is only a mutable mirror.
- CDN latest mirror is updated by CI/CD after release-artifacts succeeds, not by manual S3 copy.
- Installer behavior must stay derivable from the install script and release target manifest.
- The executable must expose the same release tag through `riido version` and `riido --version`.
- Each build uses a fresh staging directory and atomically replaces its final archive only after validation; stale helper files and failed optional-helper builds never replace a prior asset.
- Helper packaging checks fixed Apple anchor/team/identifier, hardened runtime, safe entitlements, embedded profile, executable architecture, regular paths, and exact version. Its copied archive is unpacked and verified again on macOS before publication.
- Tag releases require helper-inclusive macOS packages. The macOS CI lane consumes a pre-signed, notarized input package from the draft GitHub release, verifies the exact signed RiidoCLISourceRevision against the tag commit, helper identity/version/architecture and stapled ticket, then rebuilds the daemon from source. Pull requests may dry-run without signing credentials; they cannot publish.
- CDN verification requires the macOS helper bundle and manifest, and checks paths and versions with a portable archive validator. Apple signature and notarization are checked by the macOS build lane; neither check claims first-login presence or installation-binding acceptance.
- The standalone shell installer still installs the daemon binary only; optional helper packaging does not claim standalone auth installation support.
- Prepare each macOS input with scripts/prepare-macos-release-input.sh using the existing Apple signing identity and authorized provisioning profile. Upload riido-macos-input_darwin_{arm64,amd64}.tar.gz to a draft release targeting the reviewed main commit before pushing the tag. CI alone publishes the final release and CDN. No signing credential is uploaded in a package or copied into repository secrets.
- Both legacy flat desktop installs and managed helper installs must update to a helper-inclusive package; managed installs must continue rejecting helper removal. Real signed-package installation checks supplement fixture lifecycle tests. Busy daemons defer activation without forced termination.
